subtitle: Lesson 16 · Cybersecurity Foundations: Core Concepts

steps.label: 1. Reconnaissance
steps.sub: researching the target — employees, tech, exposed services

steps.label: 2. Weaponization
steps.sub: building the tool — malicious doc or exploit + backdoor

steps.label: 3. Delivery
steps.sub: getting it to the target — phishing email, infected USB

steps.label: 4. Exploitation
steps.sub: the weapon triggers, running code on the victim

steps.label: 6. Command & Control
steps.sub: compromised system phones home for remote commands

steps.label: 7. Actions on Objectives
steps.sub: theft, ransom encryption, or deeper pivoting

eyebrow: Break one link, stop the attack
code:
Defense doesn't require catching every stage.
It only requires breaking ONE link anywhere
in the chain to stop the attack from
reaching its final objective.
caption: Borrowed from military doctrine — the whole chain fails if any one link breaks.

steps.label: Tactic
steps.sub: the attacker's goal at a stage — e.g. "Persistence"

steps.label: Technique
steps.sub: the specific method used — e.g. a registry-key trick, each with its own ID

steps.label: Public & maintained
steps.sub: built from real documented intrusions, used industry-wide

steps.label: Kill chain answers
steps.sub: "where are we in this attack, how far have they gotten"

steps.label: ATT&CK answers
steps.sub: "exactly which technique, and what else pairs with it"

steps.label: Together
steps.sub: urgency from the kill chain, detection precision from ATT&CK
